clue.text: Lovers badly injured, lame too

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the three words after it are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has been hurt in an accident and is limping as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the fourteen letters of INJURED, LAME and TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's two star-crossed teenagers are literature's most famous pair of sweethearts.

clue.text: More than one song? That's getting blanket coverage

parts.note: over means more than, as in over a hundred
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A remark about a medley of songs getting saturation airplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlay is a covering laid over the whole of something, like a blanket.

clue.text: Free wheels before reaching pastures new

indicators.note: free signals that the letters following are released from their order and rearranged

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A cyclist coasts downhill on the way to a new life somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges WHEELS plus ERE; 'reaching' simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastures new is an idiom for a different place, somewhere other than here.

clue.text: Hands out every religious publication on Sunday

parts.note: all and every both mean the whole lot
OT is the Old Testament, a religious book

explanation.surface: Someone distributes church literature to everybody each Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or distribute portions.

clue.text: Left for dead

definitions.meaning: having gone away, as in the train has left

explanation.definitionFit: Departed means both gone away and, euphemistically, deceased.

clue.text: Within our alsatian's range

indicators.note: within tells us the letters sit inside the run of words our alsatian's

explanation.surface: How far our German shepherd dog roams.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are a mountain range dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Is deployed with chilling effect

parts.note: reads like a menacing threat, but describes a small frozen block dropped into a drink to cool it

explanation.surface: Something sinister is put to use to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen block of water is put in drinks to make them cold.

clue.text: In spite of bearing down on telepathy

parts.note: though means despite, in spite of
treading on something is pressing down on it with the feet

explanation.surface: A puzzled phrase about despite pressing down on mind-reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is the supposed ability to read another person's mind.

clue.text: Jockey turns from route and performs as expected, of course

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so these letters are jostled about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider steers off the planned route but the horse runs well on the racecourse anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' rearranges TURNS, FROM and ROUTE; the definition's 'of course' puns on a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that runs to its known form behaves as predicted, which is what of course means.

clue.text: Useful in the kitchen-the trendy, silent sort

parts.note: U means upper-class or socially acceptable, the fashionable usage

indicators.note: sort means arrange, so the letters of silent are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Describing a quiet, fashionable helper in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges SILENT to TENSIL; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement of the kind used for cooking.

clue.text: Station holds box, having removed unknown amount of substance that's inactive

parts.note: a station is a person's place or position

indicators.note: having removed signals that a letter is taken away from the word box

parts.note: box taken as written
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A depot stores a crate of some unidentified material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having removed' takes X out of BOX, leaving BO; 'holds' just joins it to PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given in trials has no active ingredient and works only through belief.

clue.text: Treats law controversially, in the main

indicators.note: something done controversially stirs things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone handles legislation in a way that upsets people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controversially' rearranges TREATS and LAW; 'the main' is an old phrase for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Briny water of the open ocean, the main, is what sea creatures live in.

clue.text: Wounded when firearm whipped out, on street

indicators.note: whipped out suggests jerking something about, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a gun is a firearm

explanation.surface: A man is hurt when a pistol is suddenly drawn on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped out' is the anagram signal; read as drawing a weapon it hides that job, and 'when' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stung is to be hurt, by a sting or by a cutting remark.

clue.text: Box does with cox

parts.note: sounds like boxing or rowing, but says that the word box matches the word cox in sound at the end

explanation.surface: A boxer sparring with the steersman of a rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that end in the same sound, like these two, are said to chime in verse.

clue.text: Worn for Seattle trip in front of Bugatti

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters are tripped up into a new order
the front of the word Bugatti is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something to wear on a journey to Seattle sitting in the front of a fancy sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges SEATTLE together with B, the first letter of Bugatti.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's safety strap is something occupants wear across the body.

clue.text: Wild bird joining domestic one using rail as a perch in this building

parts.note: a tit is a small wild bird

indicators.note: as a perch says the rail sits inside the domestic bird, like a roost

parts.note: a hen is a domestic bird
a bar is a rail

explanation.surface: A wild bird joins a farmyard one roosting on a rail in a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using ... as a perch' is the container signal. A tithe barn is a medieval barn that stored the tenth of produce owed to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn is a large farm structure once used to hold church dues.

clue.text: Rare slug rain brought out

indicators.note: brought out suggests the letters are drawn out and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: It's unusual for wet weather to make slugs appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular can mean exceptional or unusual.

annotationWithheld.clue: Beetle, after this, about to become extinct

clue.text: Girl upset, due to church

annotationWithheld.why: Girl upset, due to church: ANNA + TES (SET reversed) fits, but no clue word supplies SET unless 'upset' is both SET and its reversal signal; the printed clue may read differently

clue.text: One out of eight, possibly, gets heart attack

definitions.meaning: in a rowing eight, the oarsman setting the pace is one member of the crew
a sudden seizure of the circulation, loosely an attack of apoplexy

explanation.surface: A rower in a boat crew suffers a coronary.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke names both the pace-setting rower and a sudden seizure from a blocked blood supply.

clue.text: Drove wildly for the most part, being late

annotationWithheld.why: Drove wildly for the most part, being late: the anagram of DROVE gives OVERD, but nothing in the clue as held supplies UE; the words for the remaining letters seem missing
annotationWithheld.clue: Drove wildly for the most part, being late

clue.text: Badger has captivated the painters

indicators.note: captivated means held captive, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: taken as written
RAs are Royal Academicians, artists of the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: An animal owns a gallery of artists who are spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is crossword shorthand for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester or nag persistently.

clue.text: The one with something new, or it might be

indicators.note: it might be hints that the preceding letters can be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: Someone with a brand-new possession, or maybe not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it might be' rearranges NEW and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever possesses a thing is its proprietor.

clue.text: First mate taking soldier before magistrate

indicators.note: before places the soldier ahead of the first mate

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier
Eve was Adam's partner, the first wife in Genesis

explanation.surface: A ship's officer brings a soldier to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' looks nautical but means the first woman, Adam's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with judicial powers.

clue.text: Last of the wine: it's port

parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Finishing the bottle of wine, someone declares it to be fortified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but Gravesend is a port town on the Thames in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a town and harbour on the Thames estuary.

clue.text: Porridge going round at breakfast

parts.note: O is round in shape
taken as written
breakfast is a meal

explanation.surface: Hot cereal being passed about at the morning table.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats cooked in milk or water is a common name for this hot cereal.

clue.text: An embargo put on leave

parts.note: an gives the article A
a ban is an embargo
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A prohibition is imposed on time off.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or leave behind.

clue.text: Printers seemed bedevilled and gave a wrong impression

indicators.note: bedevilled suggests confusion, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Typesetters seemed possessed and misled the readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedevilled' rearranges PRINTERS and SEEMED; printer's devil is an old name for a print-shop apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent is to give a false account of something.
